html:
Codex adversarial implementation-plan review

Verdict

Ship with changes, as edited; do not treat the plan as an already validated system. The original plan contained literal execution blockers in models, the grader, Harbor adapter, source discovery, stakeholder state and Temporal approval/recovery. I edited the five authorized plan/control files in place, preserved the 16-task structure, and incorporated the feature-band and withheld-profile decisions that arrived during review. Project code, the spec, reference tasks and datasets were not edited. No cloud jobs or servers were started; all execution checks used temporary extracted examples.

Changelog of edits

36 change groups. P means docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-swesim-implementation.md in this commit; references below point to the edited task. The review began at commit 38cd71a; concurrent author commits updated only their own spec/notes/explainer files and are preserved. These groups aggregate related line edits rather than counting each replacement as a separate fix.

# File / task Severity fixed Edit and reason
1 Execution order and dependencies — P:13; PLAN.md:1; CLAUDE.md:1 blocking Moved register/score/export before Temporal consumers and dashboard implementation before VM service enablement; install Harbor/Modal/Temporal/test dependencies in the project environment before their imports. Removed nonexistent milestone tasks 17–19.
2 Model fixtures and serialization — P:111 (Task 1) blocking Fixed illegal two-character fact IDs, nested model updates and computed-hash JSON round trips; saving an approved spec no longer makes it fail strict reloading.
3 Model integrity — P:111 (Task 1) major Added positive finite group weights, unique/disjoint test IDs, required hidden-test assets, safe manifest paths, base SHA validation, referenced assets, and alternative-correct controls for structural tests.
4 Path and archive policy — P:495 (Task 2) blocking Replaced destructive path normalization with NFC/case folding; bounded archive members and apparent bytes; rejected traversal, duplicate/case collisions and special entries. Diff exclusions match collection exclusions.
5 Exact test IDs — P:495 (Task 2) blocking Replaced whitespace-splitting -rA parsing and guessed class paths with expected-nodeid-aware matching, explicit historical ID maps and duplicate/missing evidence rejection.
6 Actual source import — P:805 (Task 3) blocking Added the trusted -I launcher, then explicitly inserted submitted source roots after importing pytest. Preserved /testbed or /app for editable installs and the historical interpreter for tests.
7 Base and hidden overlay order — P:805 (Task 3); P:1086 (Task 4) blocking Diff against untouched prepared base first; apply candidate changes; overlay evaluator-owned assertions afterward. No-op runs execute tests and record complete base statuses.
8 Evidence reconciliation — P:805 (Task 3) blocking Require collection manifest, per-ID JUnit, terminal summary and exit-code agreement. Inconsistent evidence receives zero; fresh single-test reruns remain diagnostic instead of replacing regression evidence.
9 Receipts and patch lineage — P:805 (Task 3) major Made collect.status a validated JSON object, rejected nonzero collection results, included changed contents in patch hashes, and emitted the actual submitted text diff for review.
10 Root collection — P:1086 (Task 4) blocking Replaced flattened shell fragments with a root-owned Python collector, clean environment, explicit process termination, bounded archive construction and freeze in finally, including oversize/invalid-tree exits.
11 Prepared environments — P:1086 (Task 4) blocking Both agent and verifier consume the approved Dockerfile asset and declared context. Preserve compiled extensions/build metadata; do not replace a prepared runtime tree with git archive or git clean -ffdx. Use a pinned controller Python separately from the historical test interpreter.
12 Compiler fidelity — P:1086 (Task 4) major Verify actual asset bytes, use strict Jinja, escape TOML, require resolved/pinned base digests, package the launcher and real shims, and record a compiled content hash.
13 Harbor adapter API — P:1524 (Task 5) blocking Implemented BaseAgent.version(), used upload_file(source_path,target_path), resolved the container repository variable before quoting it, and removed the unsafe git init /tmp smoke/fallback.
14 Source pagination and evidence — P:1613 (Task 6) blocking Removed concatenated --paginate JSON parsing; fetch bounded pages, PR review bodies, issue chronology and timeline-linked issues; preserve fetch failures rather than silently losing provenance.
15 Natural brief fidelity — P:1613 (Task 6) major Keep the source problem statement verbatim. Send complete bounded authoring evidence instead of silently truncating each field; validate drafts and gate on the judge criteria before approval.
16 Applicable exploit controls — P:1613 (Task 6) blocking Build unified diffs from actual base-file contents, including existing root conftest, instead of assuming a nonexistent file or using context-free insertion hunks. Label the startup probe honestly.
17 Validation cannot pass vacuously — P:1960 (Task 7) blocking Require every F2P and P2P status on base/gold, every required control, valid non-infrastructure outcomes and nonempty reachability evidence; stale validation job reuse is prevented by compiled-hash namespaces.
18 Harbor launch/result handling — P:1960 (Task 7); P:2564 (Task 9) major Set --max-retries 0, require a unique trial result, retain agent failures, guard duplicate launches and preserve incomplete/ambiguous launch evidence instead of guessing the last directory.
19 Human approval — P:1960 (Task 7); P:2997 (Task 11); GOAL.md:1 blocking Bind approval to frozen spec/asset hashes on the execution host. The implementation agent prints the real command and waits on dependent work; a signal/path alone cannot bypass approval.
20 Durable stakeholder sessions — P:2200 (Task 8) blocking Persist session snapshots and reply caches on a Modal Volume before responses; validate session binding; persist interrupted-request state; serialize exchanges and freeze.
21 Availability and API boundaries — P:2200 (Task 8) major Fixed the final available reply and patience threshold semantics, reject reused request IDs with changed bodies, filter fact annotations to known IDs, and keep annotations out of solver-facing replies.
22 Review sandbox cut — P:2200 (Task 8) blocking Removed diff interpolation into a shell heredoc and execution before budget/cache checks by freezing the pilot to explicitly unverified diff-only review. Durable state and grading consume the saved implementation time.
23 Secrets and shims — P:2200 (Task 8); P:3527 (Task 13); CLAUDE.md:1 major Use dotenv parsing, Secret.objects.create, stable worker credentials, internal environment reads and bounded diff transport. Avoid passing provider secrets in shell arguments or copying an entire private GitHub credential store.
24 Per-trial materialization — P:2564 (Task 9) major Freeze spec/config/build inputs with each run, render the actual selected profile, align model hosts and metadata, use content-bound IDs, retain failures and mark unbound transcripts ineligible for training.
25 Repository-only feature discovery — P:2740 (Task 10) blocking Normalize GitHub URLs, fetch full PR details before statistics, count source changes, add feature/bugfix filters and the supplied shortlist with a 400-PR bound; select candidates without requiring a PR override.
26 Noncircular GitHub environment probe — P:2740 (Task 10) blocking Replaced the prose-only probe that required an already-valid ScenarioSpec with a concrete separate Harbor authoring probe over base, test overlay and gold; derive target/regression IDs and persist build failures.
27 Temporal API correctness — P:2997 (Task 11) blocking Corrected wait_condition success/timeout semantics, signal payloads, WorkflowAlreadyStartedError import, child reuse policy and model/profile-specific child IDs. Added offline branch tests and explicit server integration test code.
28 Worker restart durability — P:2997 (Task 11); P:3527 (Task 13) blocking A named user-systemd unit owns each Harbor process. Temporal launches once and polls with heartbeats; lost acknowledgement is reconciled without a fresh solver launch. Worker restart evidence must show a single launch and terminal result.
29 Statistics and registry — P:3355 (Task 12) major Preserve requested k; insufficient samples yield null. Define pass^k as C(c,k)/C(n,k), keep model/profile/purpose groups separate, deduplicate attempts, atomically register validated versions and remove the unsupported claim that dataset.toml is a Harbor input.
30 Policy-visible exports — P:3355 (Task 12) major Read the frozen per-trial spec; use recorded agent observations for policy data and place service-side disclosure annotations in evaluator-only audit. Keep unadjudicated simulator runs out of the training-ready set.
31 VM deployment — P:3527 (Task 13) blocking Ship the exact committed source archive without relying on unauthenticated private cloning, install gh, use persistent user services/linger, bind loopback, forward 7233 as well as both UIs, and retain operations evidence.
32 Viewing and example artifacts — P:3687 (Task 14); P:3787 (Task 15) major Provided a minimal actual episode viewer with deterministic timeline tests; replaced permissive/macOS-only snapshot shell commands with bounded Python copying, credential redaction, required files, submitted patch and a sanitized manifest.
33 Acceptance verifier — scripts/verify.sh:1; PLAN.md:1 blocking Replaced glob/grep/file-existence acceptance and eval-based JSON access with test execution and linked checks over controls, raw Modal configs, hashes, paired exchanges, score recomputation, registry versions, exports and cloud evidence. Invalid milestone arguments fail.
34 Goal and deadline guardrails — GOAL.md:1; CLAUDE.md:1; P:3901 major Removed arbitrary turn-based completion, unavailable skills and invented co-author requirements; keep the goal under 4,000 characters, preserve the required floor early, and name paid deferrals without checking incomplete milestones.
35 Withheld profiles across the pipeline — P:111 (Task 1); P:1086 (Task 4); P:1613 (Task 6); P:2564 (Task 9) major Applied the new user decision and pending note: category-targeted removals, original-issue excerpt facts, withholding operations, leak/title checks, bounded retry and natural/withheld profile-aware compilation/trial IDs. Full remains natural plus visible facts.
36 Paired-profile measurement — P:3355 (Task 12); scripts/verify.sh:1; GOAL.md:1 major Added profile-separated score/export records and required hidden runs with both natural and withheld briefs for at least one scenario. Synthetic removals can no longer be presented as purely natural underspecification.

Validation performed: Python fenced blocks parsed with ast.parse; executable Bash blocks and scripts/verify.sh passed bash -n; git diff --check passed. Six rendered task configs validated against the installed Harbor TaskConfig, and their collection commands passed Bash syntax checks. 57 extracted offline tests passed after the final profile changes. Tests were run from /private/tmp/swesim-plan-audit/extracted, not installed into the project. One invocation from the repository directory accidentally imported the preexisting scaffold and failed collection; rerunning from the extraction directory passed. The temporary test environment used Python 3.13; Python 3.12 and historical-image integration remain implementation checks. These results are not an oracle/agent trial and do not satisfy the delivery milestones.

Verified library calls: Harbor 0.23 BaseAgent requires version() (agents/base.py:327), its upload method is upload_file(source_path,target_path) (environments/base.py:925), ExecResult.return_code exists (environments/base.py:86), collect hooks are best-effort (trial/trial.py:1333), explicit artifacts are restored to their original source path (trial/artifact_handler.py:169), and the CLI supports --max-retries (cli/jobs.py:560). Those paths are relative to ~/.local/share/uv/tools/harbor/lib/python3.13/site-packages/harbor/. Modal 1.5.5 source confirms Secret.objects.create(...,allow_existing=True) (modal/secret.py:29), Sandbox.create(...,app=...,block_network=...) (modal/sandbox.py:569) and Function.get_web_url() (modal/_functions.py:1562); Volume.commit/reload were checked by import without calling a service. Temporal signatures were checked against the Python workflow API, signal API, test environment API, and a temporary SDK import. wait_condition returns None; duplicate-start rejection belongs to temporalio.exceptions.WorkflowAlreadyStartedError.

Findings you could not fix in the plan

Each item distinguishes a design disagreement or unverified runtime claim from an executed failure. The spec remained read-only.

  1. Major — spec §§10.2, 10.4; P Task 3: same-process report forgery remains possible. Submitted code still executes in pytest and can attack its reporting and imports. Extra files, random report names and reruns are not independent trust boundaries. Smallest verification: run an applicable malicious source patch that forges both terminal and JUnit evidence; record the result. The plan fails closed on disagreement but cannot prove agreement means correctness. Strong process-external behavioral grading would require dropping additional experimental scope.
  2. Major — spec §10.2; P Task 3: rerun authority is narrowed. The spec says to take fresh F2P rerun results on disagreement; that can hide failed/missing P2P evidence. The edited plan gives no credit to inconsistent aggregate evidence and retains reruns as diagnostics. Smallest verification: a patch that emits all-pass IDs but exits nonzero must earn zero; the spec owner must accept this stricter rule.
  3. Major — spec §§8, 10, 11; P Tasks 8/12: review hashes are not comparable. The service sees an agent-supplied textual diff; grading hashes actual source contents. The plan reports comparison as null, rather than false equality. Smallest verification: commit changes locally before requesting review and show that the reviewed text may differ from the collected tree. Restoring the specified equality metric requires a shared trusted snapshot protocol; it was deferred with check execution.
  4. Major — spec §§8, 16: HTTP response generation is not delivery evidence. A persisted service reply can be lost before the solver observes it. The plan exports actual agent trajectory observations as policy data and keeps the service log as audit. Smallest verification: drop a response after the server persists it; confirm the undelivered content does not enter policy-visible messages.
  5. Major — P Task 8: persistence APIs are verified; deployed crash recovery is not. A single Modal container plus serialized Volume commits is a pilot topology, not proof of linearizability across replacement/deployment overlap. Smallest verification: ask, redeploy/terminate the container, retry the same request ID and freeze; compare one reply, one budget debit and stable hashes. If this fails, run the same service on the already-required VM rather than adding another storage product.
  6. Major — P Tasks 4/6/10: image/runtime reproducibility is not established by the existing smoke. The smoke lacks the hardened collector and real historical dependency environment. Compiled extensions, legacy pytest/JUnit IDs, offline fixtures and editable paths vary by revision. Smallest verification: run base and gold on each selected pinned image, check imported package paths, check every exact test ID and exercise a root file-artifact round trip. Reject incompatible candidates rather than silently dropping regression IDs.
  7. Major — P Tasks 4/5; spec §§9.3, 13: reachability checks are bounded. Deleting the old git database blocks known future-object retrieval, but a few distinctive-line searches are not a complete scan for copied solutions, cached patches or memorization. Smallest verification: git cat-file -e for the actual gold SHA plus a planted solution file outside the repository; expand the image audit if that planted file is missed. Do not claim the task is unseen by a model.
  8. Major — P Tasks 9/11/13: worker restart recovery is unexecuted. API signatures and offline branch tests cannot prove a user systemd process survives service restart or that Modal results are ingested afterward. Smallest verification: interrupt the worker during one actual trial, retain the unit journal and Temporal history, and require exactly one launch plus a completed/exported record. Whole-VM loss is deliberately not claimed as transparent continuation.
  9. Major — spec §§6, 22; P Tasks 6/10: current GitHub issue bodies need not equal the issue as originally filed. The normal REST response can include edits made after resolution. Smallest verification: inspect created/updated timestamps and source history for the chosen issue; archive retrieved text and retrieval time. If original text cannot be established, label it as retrieved rather than claiming historical fidelity.
  10. Major — latest spec withholding rule; P Tasks 1/6: substring checks do not prove semantic removal. The code verifies verbatim provenance and literal excerpt absence/title retention; a paraphrase may still reveal a removed fact, or too much context may be removed. Smallest verification: human review of natural/withheld text and spans, plus a paired hidden-condition run. These are authored variants of the natural issue; do not claim natural underspecification alone caused the result.
  11. Minor — P Tasks 4/13: provider/model and deployment endpoints remain conditional. No provider model call, VM creation, Temporal binary download or Modal deployment was performed by this review. Smallest verification: one bounded request per configured provider; verify the pinned Temporal CLI archive exists; deploy/probe the stakeholder; then one actual task. Record exact resolved versions in the lockfile and run metadata.
  12. Minor — spec §7; P Task 12: dataset.toml is not verified as a Harbor interface. The installed harness has its own dataset/package models; the original TOML generator also left orphan table entries on updates. The plan now uses an explicitly swesim-owned JSON index and runs concrete Harbor task directories. Smallest verification: if publishing a Harbor dataset later, validate against Harbor's actual dataset manifest model before advertising compatibility.

Cut or deferred items and the reason

  • Executable stakeholder checks and a general agent tool loop: pay for persisted state, bounded requests and reliable grading. Diff-only review remains explicit and inspectable.
  • Third scenario, more model tiers, non-pytest source support, DeepSWE importer, multi-step/combined PR tasks and complex frontend: protect the two source paths and the reviewable example.
  • Full VM-loss recovery, automatic semantic labels, trusted review/submission equivalence and broad ranking claims: none has the required independent evidence within the trial window.
  • A 5,000-line minimum and CodeClash-style tournaments: CodeClash evaluates iterative competitive objectives. It does not establish a minimum diff size for a useful feature task. The adopted 200–1,500 source-line filter is a screening prior, with implementation difficulty still measured through agent runs.

No required milestone was waived. One task plus controls, a real interactive episode, the tracked runnable package, docs and laptop-off operation remain the minimum deliverable floor; the repo-only source and paired-profile evidence remain explicit completion requirements. Unfinished source discovery must remain unfinished in PLAN.md rather than being replaced with a manually chosen PR.

Remaining questions a reviewer of the finished project would ask

  • Which actual task requires a consequential design decision, and which baseline shows its coding difficulty rather than merely missing information?
  • Which facts come from the original report, later thread, deliberate withholding or human repair? Can each be traced to the correct source version?
  • Which attacks actually ran, did their patches apply, and which incorrect patch still earned credit?
  • What is the tested residual risk from running source code inside pytest's process?
  • Can I rerun the example from a fresh clone using only the README and declared credentials?
  • How many candidate PRs were rejected for missing fixtures, unsupported environments, weak tests or insufficient ambiguity?
  • Can the same request ID or a worker restart duplicate a reply, budget debit, solver launch or score record?
  • Which model/profile/purpose cohorts have enough attempts for the reported k? Which traces are still unadjudicated and excluded from training-ready exports?
  • Did a service reply reach the policy, or only appear in the service audit? What evidence supports each failure label?
  • Does the live page show observed events, and is delayed agent visibility clearly labeled?
